skills/agent-acceptance-gate.description: Use when about to commit or push a diff that touches two or more locale variants of one file stem, adds catalog or listing entries, states benchmark numbers, release dates, or licenses for named frontier models, or merges output from any subagent or delegate. Reconciles the lane results, runs the matching preset, and returns PASS, CONDITIONAL PASS, or FAIL with evidence.

skills/agent-context-budget.description: Use when launching parallel or background subagents, or when a handoff, log, or result would be more than a short summary (roughly 2 KB). Caps return sizes (summary in the reply, detail by path), picks a cheap model tier for mechanical lanes, records durable decisions as proposals, and checkpoints or primes a fresh session before context runs out.

skills/agent-debate.description: Use when a consequential decision has two plausible, materially different options and you are about to pick one. Runs two opposed reviewers on the same evidence with a stated round cap, then hands the human a synthesis that names the deciding evidence.

skills/agent-output-reconciler.description: Use when a plan, prompt, or doc still names agent-output-reconciler. Since 0.6.0 reconciliation is step 1 of agent-acceptance-gate; this redirect stub is removed in 0.7.0.

skills/agent-plan-act-reflect.description: Use when a plan, prompt, or doc still names agent-plan-act-reflect. Deprecated in 0.6.0; ordinary iterate-until-it-passes work needs no skill, and an unattended policy-driven loop follows agent-context-budget's harness loop reference. This stub is removed in 0.7.0.

skills/agent-shared-memory.description: Use when a plan, prompt, or doc still names agent-shared-memory. Since 0.6.0 proposal-only coordination memory is the Durable decisions section of agent-context-budget; this redirect stub is removed in 0.7.0.

skills/agent-task-splitter.description: Use when about to run two or more subagents, workflow lanes, or delegated CLI executors on one goal. Gives each lane a role, a pinned model tier, a disjoint file scope, a bounded brief, and a capped return, and fixes the merge and verification step before launch. Not for research-domain routing that owns .research, .paper, Zotero, Obsidian, or NotebookLM workflows; use research-hub-multi-ai for those.
